questions.q: If potential energy is given by $U=\frac{a}{r^2}-\frac{b}{r}$. Then find out maximum force. (Given $a=2$, $b=4)$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text {  } F=-\frac{d u}{d r}=-\left[-\frac{2 a}{r^3}+\frac{b}{r^2}\right]=\frac{2 a}{r^3}-\frac{b}{r^2} \\ & \frac{d F}{d r}=\frac{-6 a}{r^4}+\frac{2 b}{r^3}=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{6 a}{r}=2 b \Rightarrow r=\frac{3 a}{b}=\frac{6}{4}=\frac{3}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow F_{\max }=\frac{2 \times 2}{(3 / 2)^3}-\frac{4}{(3 / 2)^2} \\ & =\frac{4 \times 8}{27}-\frac{4 \times 4}{9}=\frac{32-16 \times 3}{27}=-\frac{16}{27}\end{aligned}$

Assertion : Work done in moving a body over a closed loop is zero for every force in nature.
Reason : Work done does not depend on nature of force.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.

If both assertion and reason are false.

$a=\frac{F}{m_1+m_2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle is thrown vertically upwards with velocity $11.2 \mathrm{~km} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$ from the surface of earth. Calculate its velocity at height $3 R$. Where $R$ is the radius of earth.
questions.solution:
Let a particle of mass $m$ is thrown vertically upward with velocity $v$. Let its velocity be $v^{\prime}$ at a height $3 R$ from the surface of the earth. According to the conservation of energy,
$\frac{1}{2} m v^2-\frac{G M m}{R}=\frac{1}{2} m v^{\prime 2}-\frac{G M m}{(R+3 R)}$
$v^2-\frac{2 G M}{R}=v^{\prime 2}-\frac{2 G M}{4 R}$
$v^2-v^{\prime 2}=\frac{-2 G M}{4 R}+\frac{2 G M}{R}=\frac{6}{4} \frac{G M}{R}$
$v^{\prime 2}=v^2-\frac{6}{4} \frac{G M}{R}$
$v^{\prime 2}=\sqrt{(11.2)^2-\frac{3}{2} g R} \quad\left(\because g=\frac{G M}{R^2}\right)$
$=\sqrt{(11.2)^2-\frac{3}{2} \times \frac{9.8 \times 6400}{1000}}$
$=\sqrt{(11.2)^2-(94.08)}$
$=5.6 \mathrm{~km} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$

Let a particle of mass $m$ is thrown vertically upward with velocity $v$. Let its velocity be $v^{\prime}$ at a height $3 R$ from the surface of the earth. According to the conservation of energy,
$\frac{1}{2} m v^2-\frac{G M m}{R}=\frac{1}{2} m v^{\prime 2}-\frac{G M m}{(R+3 R)}$
$v^2-\frac{2 G M}{R}=v^{\prime 2}-\frac{2 G M}{4 R}$
$v^2-v^{\prime 2}=\frac{-2 G M}{4 R}+\frac{2 G M}{R}=\frac{6}{4} \frac{G M}{R}$
$v^{\prime 2}=v^2-\frac{6}{4} \frac{G M}{R}$
$v^{\prime 2}=\sqrt{(11.2)^2-\frac{3}{2} g R} \quad\left(\because g=\frac{G M}{R^2}\right)$
$=\sqrt{(11.2)^2-\frac{3}{2} \times \frac{9.8 \times 6400}{1000}}$
$=\sqrt{(11.2)^2-(94.08)}$
$=5.6 \mathrm{~km} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A block of mass $10 \mathrm{~kg}$ is moving in $x$-direction with a constant speed of $10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. It is subjected to a retarding force $F=0.1 x$ joule/metre during its travel from $x=20 \mathrm{~m}$ to $x=30 \mathrm{~m}$. Its final K.E. will be
questions.solution:
Initial K.E., $E_1=\frac{1}{2} m v^2$
$$
=\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times(10)^2=500 \mathrm{~J}
$$
At $x=20 \mathrm{~m}$, retarding force,
$$
F_1=0.1 \times 20=2 \mathrm{~N}
$$
At $x=30 \mathrm{~m}$, retarding force,
$$
F_2=0.1 \times 30=3 \mathrm{~N} \text {. }
$$
Average Retarding Force $F=\frac{F_1+F_2}{2}=\frac{2+3}{2}=2.5$
Work done by retarding force $=$ loss in K.E.
$$
=F \times s=2.5(30-20)=25 \mathrm{~J}
$$
Final K.E. $=E_1-\operatorname{loss}$ in K.E. $=500-25=475 \mathrm{~J}$

Assertion : If momentum of a body increases by $50 \%$, its kinetic energy will increase by $125 \%$.
Reason : Kinetic energy is proportional to square of velocity.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution:
As, $p_2=p_1+50 \%$ of $p_1=(3 / 2) p_1$
$$
\therefore \quad v_2=(3 / 2) v_1
$$
As, kinetic energy, $K \propto v^2$
$$
\therefore K_2=\frac{9}{4} K_1
$$
Increase in $\mathrm{K} . \mathrm{E} .=\frac{\left(K_2-K_1\right) \times 100}{K_1}=125 \%$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A block of mass $10 \mathrm{~kg}$ is moving in $x$-direction with a constant speed of $10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{sec}$. It is subjected to a retarding force $F=-0.1 x$ joule/m eter during its travel from $x=20$ meter to $x=30$ meter. Its final kinetic energy will be
questions.solution:
According to work energy theorem,
$$
\begin{aligned}
& W=\Delta \mathrm{K} \cdot \mathrm{E} . \quad \Rightarrow W=\frac{1}{2} m v_2^2-\frac{1}{2} m v_1^2 \\
\Rightarrow & F \cdot d x=\mathrm{K} \cdot \mathrm{E} \cdot f-\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 100 \\
\Rightarrow & F \cdot d x=\mathrm{K} \cdot \mathrm{E} \cdot f-500 \\
\Rightarrow & \int_{20}^{30}-0.1 x d x=\mathrm{K} \cdot \mathrm{E} \cdot f-500 \\
\Rightarrow & -0.1\left[\frac{x^2}{2}\right]_{20}^{30}=\mathrm{K} \cdot \mathrm{E} \cdot f-500 \\
\Rightarrow & -0.1\left[\frac{900-400}{2}\right]=\mathrm{K} \cdot \mathrm{E} \cdot f-500
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\Rightarrow \mathrm{K}_{\cdot} \mathrm{E}_{\cdot f}=500-25=475 \mathrm{~J}
$$

questions.q: Three bodies, a ring, a solid cylinder and a solid sphere roll down the same inclined plane without slipping. They start from rest. The radii of the bodies are identical. Which of the bodies reaches the ground with maximum velocity?
options: All reach the ground with same velocity
questions.solution: According to conservation of mechanical energy $$ m g h=\frac{1}{2} m v^2\left(1+\frac{k^2}{R^2}\right) $$ or $v^2=\left(\frac{2 g h}{1+\frac{k^2}{R^2}}\right)$ Note : It is independent of the mass of the rolling body. For a ring, $k^2=R^2$ $$ v_{\text {ring }}=\sqrt{\frac{2 g h}{1+1}}=\sqrt{g h} $$ For a solid cylinder, $k^2=\frac{R^2}{2}$ $$ v_{\text {cylinder }}=\sqrt{\frac{2 g h}{1+\frac{1}{2}}}=\sqrt{\frac{4 g h}{3}} $$ For a solid sphere, $k^2=\frac{2}{5} R^2$ $$ v_{\text {sphere }}=\sqrt{\frac{2 g h}{1+\frac{2}{5}}}=\sqrt{\frac{10 g h}{7}} $$ Among the given three bodies the solid sphere has the greatest and the ring has the least velocity at the bottom of the inclined plane.
questions.question: Three bodies, a ring, a solid cylinder and a solid sphere roll down the same inclined plane without slipping. They start from rest. The radii of the bodies are identical. Which of the bodies reaches the ground with maximum velocity?
questions.explanation: According to conservation of mechanical energy $$ m g h=\frac{1}{2} m v^2\left(1+\frac{k^2}{R^2}\right) $$ or $v^2=\left(\frac{2 g h}{1+\frac{k^2}{R^2}}\right)$ Note : It is independent of the mass of the rolling body. For a ring, $k^2=R^2$ $$ v_{\text {ring }}=\sqrt{\frac{2 g h}{1+1}}=\sqrt{g h} $$ For a solid cylinder, $k^2=\frac{R^2}{2}$ $$ v_{\text {cylinder }}=\sqrt{\frac{2 g h}{1+\frac{1}{2}}}=\sqrt{\frac{4 g h}{3}} $$ For a solid sphere, $k^2=\frac{2}{5} R^2$ $$ v_{\text {sphere }}=\sqrt{\frac{2 g h}{1+\frac{2}{5}}}=\sqrt{\frac{10 g h}{7}} $$ Among the given three bodies the solid sphere has the greatest and the ring has the least velocity at the bottom of the inclined plane.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A block of mass $2 \mathrm{~kg} F(t) \uparrow$ is free to move along the $x$-axis. It is at rest and from $t=0$ onwards it is subjected to a timedependent force $F(t)$ in the $x$ direction. The force $F(t)$ varies with $t$ as shown in the figure. The kinetic energy of the block after 4.5 seconds is
questions.solution:
Change in momentum $=$ area under $F$ - $t$ graph
$\begin{aligned} \Delta p & =\frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 3-\frac{1}{2} \times 1.5 \times \frac{4}{3} \times 1.5 \\ & {\left[\text { Force at } 4.5 \mathrm{~s}=\frac{4}{3} \times 1.5 \mathrm{~N}\right] } \\ & =6-1.5=4.5 \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~m} \mathrm{~s}\end{aligned}$
As $\Delta p=m(v-u)=m v \quad(\because u=0)$
$\therefore \quad v=\frac{\Delta p}{m}=\frac{4.5 \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~m} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}}{2 \mathrm{~kg}}=\frac{4.5}{2} \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$
Kinetic energy of the block after $4.5 \mathrm{~s}$ is
$K=\frac{1}{2} m v^2=\frac{1}{2} \times 2 \mathrm{~kg} \times\left(\frac{4.5}{2} \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}\right)^2=5.06 \mathrm{~J}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A force $F$ acting on an object varies with distance $x$ as shown in the figure. The force is in $\mathrm{N}$ and $x$ in $\mathrm{m}$. The work done by the force in moving the object from $x=0$ to $x=6 \mathrm{~m}$ is
questions.solution:
Work done by force $=$ Area under force- displacement graph.
$=3 \times 3+\frac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 3=9+4.5=13.5 \mathrm{~J}$
